card.name: Kalbelia
card.tagline: Rajasthani snake-charmer community's serpentine women's dance
card.profile: Kalbelia is the song-and-dance tradition of the Kalbelia (Kabeliya) community of Rajasthan, formerly professional snake handlers (UNESCO). Women in flowing black skirts dance and swirl, replicating the movements of a serpent, while men accompany on the khanjari percussion and the poongi, a woodwind traditionally used to charm snakes (UNESCO). Dancers wear traditional tattoos, jewellery and garments embroidered with mirrors and silver thread; songs convey mythological stories and are improvised, transmitted orally without written texts (UNESCO).
card.insight: Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, and dancer Gulabo Sapera is among its best-known exponents (UNESCO/Indian Culture).
